definition: Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks
They help organize code and avoid repetition

examples.title: Simple Function
examples.description: A function that greets a user

examples.title: Function with Multiple Parameters

keyTakeaways: Use 'return' to send back a value

definition: Functions can accept different types of arguments
Positional, keyword, default, and variable-length arguments

examples.title: Default Arguments
examples.code:
def power(base, exponent=2):
    return base ** exponent

print(power(5))      # 25
print(power(5, 3))   # 125
explanation: exponent has a default value of 2
Can be called with or without the second argument

definition: Lambda functions are small anonymous functions
Can have any number of arguments but only one expression

examples.title: Simple Lambda
examples.description: Lambda function to add two numbers
examples.code:
add = lambda x, y: x + y
result = add(5, 3)  # 8
explanation: Takes two arguments x and y

examples.title: Lambda with Map
examples.code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
squared = list(map(lambda x: x**2, numbers))
explanation: Squares each number in the list

keyTakeaways: Often used with map, filter, reduce
